claim: A rate byte does not drive a formula. It indexes a printed table of whole steps of a twentieth of a hertz, and there are two such tables, told apart by the range the page prints against the address. The narrow one is 128 entries of 0.05 Hz, from 0.05 to 6.40. The wide one shares those entries as far as 5.00 Hz at setting 99, then steps by 0.10 to 7.00 at 119 and by 0.50 to 10.00 at 125 -- 126 entries, so the last two settings of the byte have no entry of their own and return the last one. One table serves every type: the same twenty-one slots across nineteen effect types answer to it with no per-type constant anywhere.
whyNotNamed: The tables are the claim and they are written out. A name for them would be a name for two lists of numbers, and it would suggest the lists came from somewhere this run has seen.
adds: Each record says what one slot's byte did at the settings it was asked at, and each says in as many words that no law, no table and no verdict is in it and that the printed range beside it is evidence about a page rather than about the unit. This file is where the two are joined: that the readings of twenty-one slots are one table read through nineteen effects, that the printed pair picks which of two, and that the entries are what they are. None of that is in any record, and no rerun of a stage would produce it.
refutedBy: A reading at any setting of any admissible slot that is not the entry these tables give, by more than one entry. Or a wide-range slot whose bend sits somewhere other than settings 100 and 120. Or a rate row on the page carrying a printed range that is neither of the two, which would mean there is a third table this claim does not know about.

rows: the 50 parameter rows whose data column reads 0.05 - 10.0
the 11 parameter rows whose data column reads 0.05 - 6.40

eraPriors.claim: A rate byte indexes a table the designer laid out, not a curve a routine computes.
eraPriors.why: A hundred and twenty-eight entries of two bytes cost a quarter of a kilobyte of ROM; an exponential per parameter change costs a routine the control processor of that period would rather not carry.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The 128 settings gave 128 distinct values on a smooth curve with no repeats and no change of spacing. Every setting of one slot was read: the spacing changes twice and the last two settings repeat the entry before them.

eraPriors.claim: Where a range is wider than the step can reach, the step coarsens near the top rather than the grid being made finer throughout.
eraPriors.why: Resolution is spent where a player is listening. Below five hertz a twentieth is a musical distinction; above seven it is not, and the part has no floating point to spend on either.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The wide range had turned out to be evenly divided, which is what the straight-line candidate says, or geometric. Both are in the catalogue and both lean.

alternatives.reading: The wide table has 128 entries after all, the last three of which are all 10.00 Hz, rather than 126 entries with the last two settings clamped to the end of the list.

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: The run read all three and got 9.999, 9.999 and 9.9993, within the run's own repeatability of each other.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: The two say the same thing at every setting the byte has. Nothing outside the part can tell a list that ran out from a list that ends flat, and no measurement of this unit will: the difference is in ROM, not in the air. Recording it as equivalent is the answer rather than a deferral.

alternatives.reading: The wide table's second and third steps begin somewhere other than settings 100 and 120 -- the bend is real everywhere, but its position is only measured at one slot.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The run it asked for was made and the bend is where the first slot put it. At 9 consecutive settings from 116 to 124 on 02 01 / 40 03 09 the rate is the shared table's to a worst 0.0028 Hz, which is 0.0006 octaves against a table entry of 0.021 and a margin that asked for 4. The step is a tenth of a hertz up to 119, where the rate is 7.000, and a half from 120, where it is 7.500 -- the two readings the two candidate positions differ by, and they came out on the side the first slot did. The three settings this run repeats agree with the earlier sweep of the same slot to 0.0004 Hz, so the nine are one measurement and not a second opinion about a different evening.

separatedBy.observable: The rate at settings 116 through 124 at any wide-range slot other than 01 21 / 40 03 07.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: Half a hertz at seven is 0.10 octaves. The run resolves a rate to about 0.0001 octaves take to take, and one entry of the table there is 0.021 octaves, which is the coarser floor and the one that applies.

run.why_this_slot: It already has a fifteen-point curve of its own, so the new settings join a sweep whose lower half is measured rather than standing alone, and its type prints one rate.

alternatives.reading: The step is a twentieth of a hertz everywhere, and the wider printed range is what the page says rather than what the part does.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: It leans on seventeen of the twenty-one slots. It is right on every slot the page prints 0.05 - 6.40 for and wrong above setting 99 on every slot the page prints 0.05 - 10.0 for, which is where the two tables part -- so what it establishes is that the printed range is doing work, not that it is decoration.

alternatives.reading: The printed pair are the ends of an evenly divided line in hertz.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: It leans on seventeen of the twenty-one slots, and its median residual is a thousand times the winner's. It agrees with the winner exactly on the narrow range, because 128 steps of 0.05 reach 6.40 and an even division of 0.05 - 6.40 is the same numbers; the two are separated only by the wide range, and that is where it fails.

alternatives.reading: The printed pair are the ends of a ratio scale, as an LFO usually is.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: It leans on every one of the twenty-one slots. It is the most plausible candidate on how a rate is heard and the worst on what the unit does, which is worth stating: nothing about this table was chosen for the ear.

comparedAgainst.generatedFrom: Every efx-rate record whose type and address the page prints a rate for, merged per slot: a slot asked by a four-point check, a curve and a follow-up is one slot read three times, and where two files read the same setting both readings are kept so that a disagreement between takes shows up as a residual rather than being resolved by whichever file was read last.

excluded.why: Not evidence about a rate table, and each says which of two reasons. Thirty-six sit on a type the page prints more than one rate for, and a take returns whichever modulator dominates it -- the archive's own note says nothing in the numbers says which. Four have readings that fall as the byte rises, or that the record's own controls stand behind fewer than two of. Every one of the forty is a run away from being evidence, and the run is the same one: silence the other stage.

settings.the other 20 slots: between 2 and 16 settings each, 249 readings in all

stimulus: A note held through the effect; the level and frequency of each of the take's strongest partials followed and searched for a period.
domain.outside: What the modulator's waveform is, how deep it goes and what it modulates. Whether the frequency the analysis found is the modulator's own or a multiple of it -- a triangle sweep passes each point twice per cycle, and this claim would read the same either way, so it is a claim about the table the byte indexes and not about what the LFO does with the entry. Any slot on a type with more than one modulator. Any type outside this unit.

residual.unit: share of the span the byte commands in that slot; the worst is in octaves
residual.why: None of the twenty-one slots has a residual that leans. The floor a lean is judged against here is the coarser of what the run resolved -- a few parts in a hundred thousand, take to take -- and what one entry of the table is worth, which is about two hundredths of an octave. Against the first alone every candidate leans, including the one whose entries the readings land on, because the instrument is three orders finer than the thing being identified. That is only safe because the step is measured: one slot was read at all 128 settings, so there is no room between them for entries a coarser sweep would have missed.

gates.name: gross
gates.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

gates.name: qualitative
gates.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

gates.name: power
gates.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it fails the gross gate the winner passed. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

gates.name: breakdown
gates.why: A point worse than 0.5 of the span is a failure at that point rather than error at it. A residual that leans with the setting or with frequency is pointing at a structure the model does not have; one that does not is pointing at the room and the converters, and is not made smaller by anything this project can do.

compared_against.generated_from: Every efx-rate record whose type and address the page prints a rate for, merged per slot: a slot asked by a four-point check, a curve and a follow-up is one slot read three times, and where two files read the same setting both readings are kept so that a disagreement between takes shows up as a residual rather than being resolved by whichever file was read last.

Every one of the forty is a run away from being evidence, and the run is the same one: silence the other stage.

compared_against.why_not_a_filter: The set is chosen by what a page prints, which is not in the index. A slot is in it when the document gives a rate range against that type and address, and the records of one slot are then merged -- a four-point check, a curve and a follow-up of the same slot are one slot and not three. Neither the printed range nor the merge is a property of a file's name or of a record's own fields, so a filter over the index would return the forty slots this class refuses along with the twenty-one it admits. What guards it instead is that every refusal is a queue entry: a slot that joins the set has to arrive through the admission rule, and the rule is stated where the record is read rather than here.

examples.codeHtml:
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// modulation-rate
//
// Generated by yarn sync from inferences/models/rate-stepped-table-per-printed-range.json.
// The claim it closes: inferences/roland-sc8850-01/rate-the-byte-indexes-a-printed-table.json
//
// Every constant, every section count and every structural choice below is
// the model's. The difference equations are the ordinary realisations of the
// sections the model names — this site's arithmetic, not a measurement.
//
// Compared against the unit over:
//   01 21 40 03 07: all 128
//   the other 20 slots: between 2 and 16 settings each, 249 readings in all
//   stimulus: A note held through the effect; the level and frequency of each of the take's strongest partials followed and searched for a period.
//
// Outside that domain this says nothing: What the modulator's waveform is, how deep it
// goes and what it modulates. Whether the frequency the analysis found is the modulator's
// own or a multiple of it -- a triangle sweep passes each point twice per cycle, and this
// claim would read the same either way, so it is a claim about the table the byte indexes
// and not about what the LFO does with the entry. Any slot on a type with more than one
// modulator. Any type outside this unit.
//
// Residual: 0.00145 median, 0.01013 worst, in share of the span the byte commands in that slot; the worst is in octaves.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#include <cstring>

namespace soundings::modulation_rate {

// One printed table per printed range, walked in whole steps and holding its last entry
// where the table is shorter than the byte.

// printed range: 0.05 - 10.0
// Three runs of 100, 20 and 6 come to 126 entries, so settings 126 and 127 have no entry
// of their own and return the last one.
// a ladder of 126 entries from 0.05 in 3 run(s)
inline double at005100(int byte) {
  static const int kThrough[] = {99, 119, 125};
  static const double kStep[] = {0.05, 0.1, 0.5};
  constexpr int kRuns = sizeof(kThrough) / sizeof(kThrough[0]);
  // 126 entries: past the last one the byte returns what the last one holds.
  const int wanted = byte < 126 ? byte : 125;
  double value = 0.05;
  for (int index = 1; index <= wanted; ++index) {
    for (int run = 0; run < kRuns; ++run) {
      if (index <= kThrough[run]) { value += kStep[run]; break; }
    }
  }
  return value;
}

// printed range: 0.05 - 6.40
// a ladder of 128 entries from 0.05 in 1 run(s)
inline double at005640(int byte) {
  static const int kThrough[] = {127};
  static const double kStep[] = {0.05};
  constexpr int kRuns = sizeof(kThrough) / sizeof(kThrough[0]);
  // 128 entries: past the last one the byte returns what the last one holds.
  const int wanted = byte < 128 ? byte : 127;
  double value = 0.05;
  for (int index = 1; index <= wanted; ++index) {
    for (int run = 0; run < kRuns; ++run) {
      if (index <= kThrough[run]) { value += kStep[run]; break; }
    }
  }
  return value;
}

/**
 * Which table applies is decided by the range the page prints against the
 * address, which is a fact about the document rather than about the byte.
 */
inline bool lookUp(const char* printedRange, int byte, double& out) {
  if (std::strcmp(printedRange, "0.05 - 10.0") == 0) { out = at005100(byte); return true; }
  if (std::strcmp(printedRange, "0.05 - 6.40") == 0) { out = at005640(byte); return true; }
  // A range no reading has been taken over. Saying nothing is the answer:
  // returning a neighbouring table would be inventing a measurement.
  return false;
}

}  // namespace soundings::modulation_rate

extra.key: a note on what was left out
extra.text: Twenty-eight readings of the twenty-one admissible slots were left out by the records' own controls: a figure fewer than half the take's partials found, or a figure at or under the slowest rate the take was long enough to carry. Both exclusions are stated per reading in the run and neither looks at any model. The second is the one that matters: a take too short returns its analysis floor at every setting, which is stable, and stable is what makes it look like a byte that does nothing.

extra.key: rows that declined after this was made
extra.text: Three of the rows this rests on stopped naming a rate. The reading that made them was changed to refuse a take whose partials split evenly between two rates rather than resolve it, and at settings 116, 120 and 124 of this byte two partials fall on one rate and two on another. What the rows publish now is the pair. In all three the higher of the pair is the entry this claim reads off the printed table -- 6.70, 7.50 and 9.50 hertz -- and the lower stands to it as one to 2.999, 3.000 and 3.001, which is two partials followed at every third cycle rather than a second modulation. So the rows are still the rows this claim was made on and the thing that chooses between the branches is the printed table, which is where a choice of that kind belongs. The neighbouring settings decide it independently: 117, 118, 119, 121, 122 and 123 name a rate outright and sit on the same two steps, of a tenth below 119 and a half above it, so a table built from the six that did not split predicts all three that did.
